content.title: About
content.content: Naan is a traditional Indian flatbread baked in a tandoor at very high heat. The dough is usually made from wheat flour, water, yeast, salt and sometimes yogurt or ghee, giving the crust a crisp bite and the interior a soft, slightly aromatic texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Naan is often served hot, brushed with butter right after baking.
A tandoor is a clay oven that can reach temperatures of 400 °C, imparting a distinctive smoky flavor and cooking the bread from both sides simultaneously.
There are many variations: garlic naan, cheese naan, naan topped with sesame or poppy seeds.
In India naan is traditionally eaten with curry, dal or kebabs, using it as a “spoon” for sauces.
The word “naan” comes from the Persian “nan,” meaning “bread.”

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Naan provides a quick source of energy thanks to its high content of complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Wheat flour in naan supplies plant‑based protein important for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dough contains B1, B2 and niacin, which support metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Naan provides iron, magnesium and phosphorus, essential for bone health and blood formation.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Its thin structure and small crumb size aid rapid digestion.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Naan contains gluten, so it should be avoided by people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because it can raise blood sugar quickly, people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Traditional recipes often include salt; the amount can be reduced if needed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve naan hot, tear or cut into pieces and brush with butter. It can be used as a base for sandwiches, wrapped around meat, vegetables or sauces, and as a “spoon” for curries and gravies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh naan in a paper bag at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, wrap tightly in foil and refrigerate for up to 5 days or freeze in an airtight bag for up to 2 months.
